rule: one namespace, a space per binding
why: a parameter, a loop variable, a function or a local that holds no module names no type

rule: one namespace, a space per binding
why: a type used as a value is the table of its functions, which the program cannot use as a value of the type

rule: one namespace, a space per binding
why: a primitive type name is never a binding, so a type declared with one would be unreachable

rule: a name is declared once where it is visible
why: a declaration whose name is visible hides the earlier one, and a reader takes the first for the second
a statement after `return` never runs, and a `return` that has no statement to end is a mistake of the program
a byte that begins no token is no part of the language, so the rest of the line cannot be read

only a name or a parenthesized expression takes a call, an index or a field, as in Lua
a comma separates two items, so one with nothing after it is a mistake

a token no statement begins with is a mistake of the program

rule: types may be declared later in a signature or a type
why: a type name that no binding, declared global or primitive holds names no type

why: a name that no binding and no declared global holds reads nil at run time, so the typo is found where it is written
a long comment without its closing bracket runs to the end of the file and hides every statement after it
